decisions.selected: Adoption-time intent (commit 9b89368509e8c0a5520d90448853ad28bcece346, PR #29111) is to make .github/aw and .github/agents instruction files more concise without losing technical accuracy, batching 5 files per daily run and opening a pull request only when genuine improvements are found.
alternatives: Treat the workflow as an activity/output-volume producer (files touched per run) rather than an outcome producer.
decisions.rationale: The workflow's own description and body text ('make instruction files ... more concise ... without degrading usefulness') state a durable-content-reduction outcome, not an activity count.

decisions.selected: The opportunity is the pull request opened by a given run's safe-output job for its round-robin batch of instruction files.
alternatives: Aggregate corpus-wide line-count of all eligible instruction files as a single always-overlapping repository-health case.
decisions.rationale: Per-PR assignment avoids diluting the signal with unrelated commits that touch the same directories for other reasons, and keeps ownership close to non-overlapping (one PR per run, per repository convention of one create-pull-request safe-output call per run).

decisions.selected: Reconstruct the assigned PR by searching merged/open pull requests titled with the safe-output's configured title-prefix ('[caveman] '), labelled documentation/automation/prompt-quality, authored by github-actions[bot], created within [run.createdAt, run.createdAt+3h); ties broken by earliest created_at then lowest PR number.
alternatives: Match by an embedded gh-aw-workflow-id/run-id HTML comment in the PR body (the repo-wide safe-outputs footer convention).
Match by PR head branch name pattern (caveman-optimize-<date>-<hash>).
decisions.rationale: Verified against real PRs (#57777, #56727) that a separate always-on workflow, pr-description-caveman (.github/workflows/pr-description-caveman.md, triggers on every merged PR except signed/jsweep and copilot branches), rewrites merged PR bodies and destroys the original gh-aw-workflow-id/run-id footer marker, making body-marker matching unreliable. Branch names carry an agent-chosen hash suffix that cannot be derived from run metadata. Title/label/author/time-window matching survived body rewrites in both inspected examples and is bounded by the observed near-immediate (minutes to hours) gap between run start and PR creation for this workflow.
evidenceReferences: PR github/gh-aw#57777 (title and labels intact after merge, body rewritten)
PR github/gh-aw#56727 (footer replaced with pr-description-caveman's own marker)
workflow run 33556938804 created_at 2026-09-01T20:43:00Z vs PR #57777 created_at 2026-09-01T20:51:05Z

decisions.selected: Accept the PR's own files API (deletions/additions) as the claimed line reduction for eligible paths (.github/aw/**.md, .github/agents/**.md), and accept git-evidence line counts of those same paths at the merge commit and at the evidence-cutoff commit as proof the reduction persisted (was not reverted).
alternatives: Accept only whether the PR merged (binary), ignoring whether the reduction survived subsequent commits.
decisions.rationale: A merged-but-later-reverted trim (evidenced e.g. by closed-unmerged sibling PRs #40158, #29246 showing this workflow's PRs do sometimes get closed rather than accepted) would falsely count as full attainment under a merge-only rule; durability against reverts is the more direct signal of accepted, accuracy-preserving conciseness gains.

decisions.selected: Maturation is a fixed 7 days (604800s) after run.createdAt.
decisions.rationale: The workflow's own safe-output config expires unmerged PRs after 3 days (safe-outputs.create-pull-request.expires: 3d); 7 days gives that expiry window time to resolve plus a buffer to observe whether a merged reduction is reverted.

decisions.selected: primaryMetric id pr-reduction-durability: reductionClaimed = sum(deletions-additions) over the PR's eligible files; if unmerged, value=0; else value = clamp((reductionClaimed - growthSinceMerge)/reductionClaimed, 0, 1), where growthSinceMerge is the net line-count change of those same paths between the merge commit and the evidence-cutoff commit.
alternatives: Score by raw line-count delta against an arbitrary fixed target (e.g. reduce toward a fixed target-lines threshold), as daily-file-diet does for Go files.
Score corpus-wide aggregate conciseness (total eligible instruction lines) rather than the run's specific assigned files.
decisions.rationale: Markdown instruction files have no established compiler-enforced size convention analogous to daily-file-diet's 1000/500 Go-line thresholds, so an arbitrary target-lines value would not be defensible from adoption-time evidence. Anchoring the target to the PR's own claimed reduction and measuring only its durability keeps the metric direct, bounded in [0,1], and free of an invented threshold, while still rewarding higher-magnitude trims that survive.

alternatives: Score pre-adoption manual instruction-trimming commits, if any existed, as a comparable baseline.
decisions.rationale: No automated or manual round-robin instruction-conciseness effort existed in this repository before the adoption commit; the workflow introduced this behavior from scratch, so there is no comparable pre-adoption evidence to freeze as a baseline.
evidenceReferences: commit 9b89368509e8c0a5520d90448853ad28bcece346 (first commit adding the workflow, no prior similar automation found)

decisions.selected: diagnosticMetric batch-size-ratio: min(1, eligibleFileCount/5), reported separately from the primary value.
decisions.rationale: The workflow's own documented batch size is 5 files per run; reporting how much of that target batch a given PR actually covers gives normalized context on run scope without being combined into the durability metric.
evidenceReferences: .github/workflows/daily-caveman-optimizer.md:157 (Pick the next 5 files ... this is your batch for this run)

uncertainties.description: The time-window PR search (title/label/author, 3-hour window) could match the wrong PR if a manual workflow_dispatch run and the daily cron run both produce a caveman PR within the same window on the same day, or if title/label conventions change.
GitHub search/issues and pulls/files API calls can fail transiently (rate limiting, outages); such failures are surfaced as null rather than a score.
Line counts are computed via newline counting (wc -l / git blob content); files without a trailing newline or with unusual line endings could be off by one line.

Growth in the assigned files' line counts after merge could come from unrelated commits (e.g. schema updates, new examples) rather than a genuine revert of this run's specific trim, so a low durability score does not prove the trim itself was rejected.
attainment-only baseline means no pre-adoption comparison point exists; scores can only be interpreted in absolute terms, not relative to a prior state of the repository.
The 7-day maturation window is a design choice calibrated from the 3-day PR expiry plus buffer, not derived from a formal distribution of historical merge-to-revert times.
